paper_metadata.title: A high performance Mg–Al–Ca alloy processed by high pressure die casting: Microstructure, mechanical properties and thermal conductivity

evidence.quote: Here, we report a high performance Mg–7Al–3Ca (AX73, wt.%) alloy with high strength, good thermal conductivity, and acceptable heat resistance via the high-pressure die casting (HPDC) method.
To solve the above-mentioned problems, HPDC Mg–Al–RE system alloys, such as AE42 (Mg–4Al–2RE) and AE44 (Mg–4Al–4RE), are developed and studied in the past few years
The HPDC Mg–Al based alloys, such as AZ91 (Mg–9Al–1Zn, wt.%) and AM60 (Mg–6Al–0.3Mn, wt.%), are commonly used
The thermal conductivity of Mg alloys is sensitive to the composition.
Compared to the RE-containing HPDC Mg alloys (AE44 and AE42), the AX73 and AX73-T5 alloy exhibit much higher strength but lower thermal conductivity.
the AZ91D alloy has the lowest electrical conductivity.
The microstructure and phase constituent of the AX73 alloy subjected to aging treatment, which is named AX73-T5, are also investigated and presented in Fig. 6.

The prepared raw materials with a total quantity of 40 kg were completely melted in a resistance furnace under the protection of N2 and SF6 in a steel crucible, where the melting temperature was ~710 ◦C.
The melts were held at ~690 ◦C for 30 min before HPDC.

parameters.cooling_method: steel mold with oil heating/cooling at 280 °C

evidence.quote: The HPDC was conducted on the IMPRESS DCC280T cold-chamber machine using a steel mold equipped with an oil heating/cooling system, which was used to control the die temperature and set to 280 ◦C. The detail parameters used in the present study were as follow: pouring temperature, ~690 ◦C; injection pressure, 50 MPa; ram velocity, 1.5 m s 1; die holding time, ~3–4 s.
The aging treatment was conducted by using the tensile bars, where the tensile bars were kept at 200 ◦C for 2 h followed by air cooling.
